summary: Holmes County tower reported in May 1950 as contracted, per a Panama City paper quoted on a lookout site; no source found confirms completion or describes the site now.

facts.status_note: The only source is a May 1950 newspaper report that a contract had been let and construction was to start. No source confirms the tower was finished or still stands.

events.note: The Panama City News-Herald reported in May 1950 that a contract had been let for the tower and that construction would start immediately. The report does not confirm completion.

evidence.supports: Tower planned at Wright's Creek north of Bonifay, a Florida Forest Service lookout
evidence.quote: a contract has been let for the construction of a Florida Forest Service lookout tower at Wright's Creek north of Bonifay

evidence.supports: Announcement came from District Forester J. Edwin Moore, of Panama City
evidence.quote: District Forester J. Edwin Moore, of Panama City, announced this week

evidence.supports: Report date is May 30, 1950, from the Panama City News-Herald
Construction was slated to start immediately
evidence.quote: with construction slated to start immediately.

evidence.supports: A second tower was expected before July 1, giving Holmes County two lookout stations
evidence.quote: A second tower is expected to be erected before July 1, giving Holmes county two lookout stations from which forest fires will be detected.

evidence.supports: Towers were to have two-way radio
evidence.quote: The towers will be equipped with two-way radio for rapid communication with fire-fighting trucks and ranger headquarters.

evidence.supports: Active fire suppression was to start shortly after July 1
evidence.quote: Active forest fire suppression will start shortly after July 1.

sources.title: Wrights Creek - Forest Lookouts (quoting the Panama City News-Herald, May 30, 1950)

notes_for_editor: One newspaper report, quoted on a lookout hobby site. No source found confirms that the tower was finished, when it came down, or who ran it after 1950. Searches found only topo-map listings with name and coordinates. The story is short because the evidence is one report of a contract and construction still to come.
